pending_findings.summary: registerWalkIn() in src/modules/queue/index.ts still computes a publicDisplayLabel(entryId) derived directly from the queue entry's own UUID and passes it into the queue_entries INSERT, violating Issue #49 req #2 ('do not derive labels directly from... database IDs'). db/migrations/0007's BEFORE INSERT trigger unconditionally overwrites it with a safe random value before the row is persisted -- empirically verified against real Postgres (hand-inserted the insecure value, trigger overwrote it) -- so there is no live PII/correlation leak today, but the dead insecure code path is a latent regression risk: a future removal of the trigger (plausible as a 'redundant cleanup') would silently reintroduce ID-derived public labels, and the current test suite only checks the final persisted value so would not catch that regression.
pending_findings.required_resolution: Delete the publicDisplayLabel(entryId) helper and its call site in registerWalkIn; stop passing a computed value into the public_display_label column of that INSERT (omit the column or pass NULL/DEFAULT) and rely entirely on the migration 0007 trigger to assign it -- loadRegistration's existing re-select already reads back the correct value with no other change needed.
pending_findings.verification_method: grep -n "publicDisplayLabel(" src/modules/queue/index.ts shows zero call sites after the fix (function removed); existing tests/integration/waiting-room-public.test.ts (3 tests) continues to pass unchanged since it only exercises the final persisted/returned label; independent re-verification against real Postgres before re-gating.

resolved_findings.resolution: service_order fully removed (column, index, every code reference) per ChatGPT's ARCHITECTURE_DECISION; priority_order is now the sole authoritative override using the pre-existing queue_entries_session_priority_uq index. call()/listOperational() order by priority_order-cohort-first then eligibility_order/registration_order, matching ARCHITECTURE.md:96-108. reorder()'s active cohort is state IN (waiting,checked_in) AND priority_order IS NOT NULL with correct 1..N+1 insert / 1..N move bound differentiation. Lifecycle exits (call/no_show/cancel) compact the remaining priority cohort to contiguous 1..N via the same NULL-first-then-assign pattern from CLAUDE-031, now correctly reused for priority_order in both reorder() and command()'s own compaction block. queue_order_version now advances on every cohort-affecting lifecycle command, not just reorder() (closing the standing Codex P1 finding from the first commit). UI removed all service_order references and forces an authoritative reload after every command/reorder instead of optimistic client-side sorting. Independently re-verified against real Postgres: 3 consecutive full-suite runs (34/34), typecheck/lint/format/unit+API clean, plus a fresh adversarial test inducing a priority-cohort gap via command()'s own compaction path and reordering through it -- succeeds, deterministic, no raw 23505. CI (run 34053605419) confirmed tied to this exact head, all green. One non-blocking NOTE: command()'s compaction block lacks the try/catch around 23505 that reorder()'s equivalent has; verified not exploitable since both paths sit behind the same session-row lock, but a consistency nit worth a follow-up.

Added reason: 'Patient left before being called' to the no_show command() call in the gap-regression test. Independently verified: diffed the two heads to confirm this was the only application/test change, then ran the full integration suite 3 consecutive times against real Postgres from a clean worktree (34/34 every run, all five files), plus typecheck/lint/format and unit+API. GitHub CI (run 34051506983) independently confirmed tied to this exact head, all green.

reorder() now bulk-sets service_order=NULL for the whole locked checked-in cohort (UPDATE ... WHERE id=ANY($1::uuid[])) before assigning final contiguous 1..length values, structurally removing every touched row from the partial unique index before any new value is written -- eliminating the gap-collision case entirely rather than relying on a safe offset. Also wraps the update in a try/catch translating 23505 to QueueConflictError as defense in depth. Independently re-verified: re-ran the original real-Postgres repro (check in 3, no_show the middle one, check in a 4th, reorder the first entry to the back) against this exact head in a fresh worktree -- it now succeeds with deterministic service_order [1,2,3], where it previously threw a raw 23505.
